director_audit.rule_reading: The pre-registered 50%-of-copies letter was statistically naive: at a zero-mean site the <=0 fraction of 100 copies is binomial with sigma ~5%, so 56/47/43% are all within 1.4 sigma of 50% and ~40 sigma from a sky pixel's ~1%. Intent of the rule (no hole on a sky pixel) MET for all three; letter NOT MET for two — recorded as a flaw of the rule, not softened after the fact.
director_audit.verdict: stage 3 FIT TO LAND: no sky hole; 3 pits of 23,033,467 px, R only, each 1 px beside a bright star; the same pits existed under -output_norm (shifted positive by mu, one of them mapped to exactly 0 as the product's darkest pixel). A pedestal would keep a resampling artefact as negative data and add a non-physical offset to the whole product — not adopted.
